headline: Volume has plateaued in a tight band for eight weeks, but yesterday's LT test at 4:24/km @ 178 bpm gives you a concrete aerobic quality anchor to build interpretation around going forward.
summary:
The four-week rolling numbers tell a clean story: 127 km across 9 runs versus 125 km and 9 runs the prior block — essentially identical structure, not a coincidence. This isn't stagnation; it's a stable platform, and at ~32 km/week with the commute load sitting underneath it, the actual aerobic stimulus is meaningfully higher than the tracked numbers suggest. What's notable is that this consistency is being maintained across a range of effort types, from yesterday's easy 13.77 km at 5:48/km through to the 15.73 km at 4:49/km on June 27th, which at HR 161 represents genuine threshold-adjacent work.

The June 27th effort is worth holding onto as a reference point: 15.73 km at 4:49/km average with 70m elevation is a solid quality run, and sitting close to your LT pace territory given the test result of 4:24/km. That test itself — conducted the following day after a 13.77 km effort — gives you your first hard data point for threshold fitness in this training block. A 30-day baseline is still accumulating, so treat 4:24/km @ 178 bpm as a marker to compare future tests against rather than a verdict on current form.

Strength consistency is the one area worth watching structurally: 4 sessions in the last four weeks against a year-to-date average of 1.3/week suggests the recent streak of 3 weeks is a positive correction rather than a settled pattern. Your demonstrated strength numbers are substantial — 130 kg RDL, 16 pull-ups BW — and maintaining that base requires enough session frequency to avoid slow erosion, particularly given the running volume sitting alongside it.
watch_items: Monitor whether the LT pace (4:24/km) holds or improves as you accumulate more threshold test data points over the coming weeks — this is the primary fitness signal to track right now
